explanation.definitionFit: Satinwood is a hard, lustrous timber used in fine cabinet-making, a material with a smooth sheen.

clue.text: Tangy M&S shakes in tumbler?

indicators.note: shaking something jumbles it, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tangy drink from Marks & Spencer, a British high-street store, being shaken in a glass tumbler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tumbler' suggests a glass to go with the shakes; the question mark flags the other sense, someone who does somersaults.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is an acrobat who performs flips and rolls, which is what a gymnast does on the floor.

clue.text: Scrabble game's front runner?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrabble' with a capital looks like the board game; here it is the verb, to scratch about.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrabble is to feel about with the hands, which is to grope for something.

clue.text: One having severe dips apparently

explanation.surface: Someone who suffers deep lows.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: 'manic' is the kind of word that signals rearranging, and DEPRESSIVE rearranged gives 'severe dips'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with bipolar disorder swings between highs and deep lows of mood, the severe dips of the clue.

clue.text: 9 won't start crying, which is odd

clue.text: Protecting area, utterly stupid guards

clue.text: Lie in vehicle's trunk

clue.text: Most awkward deity one found in home

clue.text: Fish 'n' chips starter to feed A&E maybe

clue.text: Sort of pink and black stuff across river

parts.note: coal is the black fuel dug from mines

clue.text: Play review may have this done

definitions.text: Play review may have this done

parts.words: Play review may have this done

explanation.surface: A critic's notice of a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as CAST RATED, it describes what a play review does; as one word, it is what 'having it done' means for a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being neutered, 'done' in the pet-owner's euphemism, is the same as being gelded.

clue.text: Soldiers welcoming hesitant wash Saturdays/Sundays?

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service regiment
a stammered bath, with the first letter said twice as B-BATH

clue.text: Boat loads produce paid for before dispatch

to form something is to make or produce it

explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma invoice is sent so goods are paid for in advance of delivery.

clue.text: A railway crossing sensitive area, soil used in heavy farming

parts.note: the groin is a tender part of the body
dust is fine dry earth

explanation.surface: A railway line laid over tender ground whose soil is worked by intensive farming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' places A ... RY on either side of GROIN and DUST.

clue.text: Yes, that's Russian camouflage material

clue.text: I'll save part of junk

clue.text: Fine material for singer?

clue.text: Battle-axe given name again? It never needs one
